name: Push notifications
explanation: Messages sent to a user's phone or browser even when the app is closed, using services such as Firebase Cloud Messaging or the Web Push API.
triggers: notify their phone;notification to their phone;app is closed;send a notification;phone notification
requirements: Ask for permission only after the user sees the value, never on page load;Let users choose which kinds of notifications they get;Remove expired or invalid device tokens;Keep messages short, and link each one to the right screen;Keep sensitive data out of the notification text
done_when: Users can turn off each kind of notification;Tapping a notification opens the matching screen

name: Touch gestures
explanation: Swipes, pinches, long presses and device motion used to control an app on touch screens.
synonyms: gestures;swipe;pinch to zoom;long press;shake to undo
triggers: swipe to delete;swipe left;swipe between;pinch to zoom;long press menu;shake the phone;tilt the phone
requirements: Offer a single-tap alternative, such as a button, for swipes, pinches and other path or multi-finger gestures;Trigger actions when the finger lifts, so users can cancel by sliding away;Offer buttons for actions triggered by shaking or tilting, and let users turn motion control off;Make touch targets at least 24 by 24 pixels, ideally 44;Never block the browser's own pinch to zoom;Give visible feedback while a gesture is in progress
done_when: Every gesture action can also be done with a single tap or click;Pinch to zoom works on every page

name: Mobile app security
explanation: Protecting data and secrets in iOS and Android apps, which run on devices you do not control.
triggers: mobile app;ios app;android app;store tokens on the phone;react native app;flutter app
requirements: Keep tokens in the iOS Keychain, or encrypted with an Android Keystore key, never in plain files or preferences;Never put API secrets in the app, because apps can be decompiled;Use HTTPS for every request, and consider certificate pinning for high-risk apps;Check authorization on the server, never trusting checks in the app;Keep sensitive data out of logs, backups, screenshots and the app switcher;Validate deep links, intents and other IPC, and export only components that must be public;In WebViews, turn off JavaScript and file access unless needed, and load only trusted URLs;Tie biometric unlock to a key in the Keychain or Keystore, not just a yes or no result
done_when: Decompiling the app reveals no secrets;Data stored on the device is protected by the platform keystore

name: Mobile app hardening
explanation: Making a mobile app harder to tamper with, reverse engineer, or run on compromised devices, for apps that handle money or sensitive data.
triggers: rooted phone;jailbroken;stop people modifying the app;protect the app code;force app update;minimum os version;banking app
requirements: Check device and app integrity with Play Integrity or App Attest, verified on the server;Detect rooted or jailbroken devices, and limit risky features on them;Obfuscate code and strip debug information in release builds;Detect debuggers and tampering, and react on the server, not only in the app;Require a supported, up-to-date operating system version;Be able to make users update to a fixed version;Treat these as extra layers: the server must stay safe even if the app is fully compromised
done_when: A modified or re-signed app is detected by the server;Users of outdated, unsafe versions are made to update

name: Bottom sheet
explanation: A panel that slides up from the bottom of a phone screen to show options or details, and can often be dragged up or down.
triggers: panel from the bottom;slides up from the bottom;drag up panel;sheet from the bottom;pull up menu;mobile options menu
requirements: Give it a close button as well as a drag handle, because not everyone can swipe;Close it with Escape, the back button or gesture, and a tap on the backdrop;Treat a sheet that blocks the screen as a modal dialog for focus and screen readers;Respect safe-area insets so content is not hidden behind the home indicator;Snap to clear heights, such as half and full screen;Let long content scroll inside the sheet without closing it
done_when: It can be closed without a swipe gesture;Scrolling inside the sheet never closes it by accident;Content is never hidden under the phone's home bar

name: Floating action button
explanation: A round button that floats over the content, usually in the bottom corner of a mobile screen, for the main action such as New message.
triggers: plus button;bottom right corner;round button bottom right;floating add button;button that floats;button in the bottom corner
requirements: Use it only for the single most important action on the screen;Give it a clear accessible name, such as New message, not just a plus icon;Make it at least 48 by 48 pixels and keep it away from other controls;Make sure it never covers content, such as the last item in a list;Respect safe-area insets on phones with notches or home bars;Put it in a sensible place in the keyboard order
done_when: Screen readers announce what the button does;It never hides the last item in a list;It can be reached and used with the keyboard

name: Bottom navigation bar
explanation: A row of icons with labels along the bottom of a mobile app screen, used to switch between its main sections.
synonyms: bottom tab bar;bottom nav;tab bar navigation;mobile tab bar
triggers: icons at the bottom;menu at the bottom of the screen;bottom menu;mobile app navigation;tabs at the bottom;app sections at the bottom
requirements: Use three to five main sections, each with an icon and a short text label;Mark the current section with aria-current and a visible style;Keep it visible and in the same order on every main screen;Make each target at least 48 by 48 pixels;Respect the safe area so it sits above the home indicator;Keep each section's scroll position and state when switching back
done_when: Users can always tell which section they are in;Icons are never shown without labels;Switching sections keeps each one where the user left it

name: Pull to refresh
explanation: Refreshing a list by dragging it down from the top and letting go, common in mobile apps and feeds.
synonyms: swipe to refresh;pull down to refresh;drag to refresh
triggers: down to reload;down to refresh;pull down to reload;drag down to refresh;refresh the feed;refresh by pulling;pull the list down
requirements: Start refreshing only when the user pulls down at the top of the list;Show a clear indicator while pulling and while loading;Offer another way to refresh, such as a button or automatic updates;Stop the browser's own pull-to-refresh with overscroll-behavior when building a custom one;Show an error with a retry option if refreshing fails;Keep the scroll position when new items arrive
done_when: Pulling at the top refreshes, and scrolling elsewhere never does;Users who cannot swipe can still refresh;A failed refresh shows a clear message
